BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p570/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p570/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p570/r2.claim: The phrase occurs in the Quranic reward passages in al-Qalam, Fussilat, al-Inshiqaq, and al-Tin; the root mann occurs sixteen times, as does the phrase r-rayb al-manun in al-Tur.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p570/r2.anchor: ومعها (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ) فى آيات.

DAMGHANI:v1p443/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p443/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p443/r8.claim: Mamnūn means cut off, so an ajr ghayr mamnūn is an unending reward.
DAMGHANI:v1p443/r8.anchor: (( لهم اجر غير ممنون )) يعنى غير مقطوع

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r2.claim: Those adamant in rejecting the Qur'an are warned, while believers who do righteous deeds receive glad tidings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r2.anchor: doing righteous deeds after affirming the warnings

BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqāq continues the close of al-Muṭaffifīn: allies enjoy reward and enemies receive punishment because they denied resurrection and judgment before their Creator-King.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر المطففين من أن الأولياء ينعمون والأعداء يعذبون ، لأنهم كانوا لا يقرون بالبعث ولا بالعرض على الملك الذي أوجدهم ورباهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r8.claim: Belief is confession and righteous deeds demonstrate its truth; their reward is God’s great bounty, including pardon and concealment of minor sins, never ending, diminishing, or reproachful.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r8.anchor: أي عظيم وثواب جزيل يعلمه الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r9.claim: Deeds do not truly cause the reward, which rests on enveloping mercy; omission of the causal fa signals this, unlike the context of Surat al-Tin.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r9.anchor: أسقط الفاء المؤذنة بالسبب تنبيها على ذلك بخلاف ما في سورة التين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p459#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p459#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p459#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says mamnun means counted, reckoned against them, or diminished by reminders of the favor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p459#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ممنون، بمعنى: معدود عليهم محسوب منغص بالمن.

ZAJJAJ:v5p305/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p305/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p305/r8.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means an unmerited reward for which they are not reproached; another view means it is uncut or unending, as manaytu means I cut the rope.
ZAJJAJ:v5p305/r8.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: غير ممنون غير مقطوع، يقال منيت الحبل إذا قطعته.

STUDYQURAN:84:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:intro/r3.claim: The surah moves from Judgment Day events to contrasting reckonings, then oaths, and finally the different ends of believers and disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:84:intro/r3.anchor: The sūrah begins with allusions to events that will transpire on the Day of Judgment

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r23.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r23.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r23.claim: Al-Inshiqāq spends many verses on disbelievers and their punishment but says little about believers, so omitting fa suits its concise reward statement.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r23.anchor: فانظر كيف أطال في وصف الكافرين وأعمالهم وعقابهم، وأوجز في الكلام على المؤمنين

BURSEVI:v10p296/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p296/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p296/r4.claim: Kashifi says the threat also hints at believers’ bodily and spiritual comfort in reward; ‘except those who believe’ is a disconnected exception, placing believers outside the unbelievers addressed.
BURSEVI:v10p296/r4.anchor: يعني خبركن ايشانرا بعذاب دردناك وفيه رمز إلى تبشير المؤمنين بالثواب

BURSEVI:v10p296/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p296/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p296/r5.claim: The faithful have sincere belief, including knowledge that cleanses hearts of the self’s traits, and righteous deeds that include commanded worship and acquisition of virtues.
BURSEVI:v10p296/r5.anchor: إيمانا صادقا وأيضا الإيمان العلمي بتصفية قلوبهم عن كدر صفات النفس

BURSEVI:v10p296/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p296/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p296/r6.claim: Their reward is unbroken and enduring; ‘not bestowed as a favor’ is another possible meaning, though uninterrupted reward is more apparent, since even the capacity and guidance to act are God’s favor.
BURSEVI:v10p296/r6.anchor: أي غير مقطوع بل متصل دائم من منه منا بمعنى قطعه قطعا

BURSEVI:v10p296/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p296/r7.speaker: حسن البصري
BURSEVI:v10p296/r7.claim: Hasan al-Basri recalls people who gave away worldly wealth generously without reminding recipients of their favor.
BURSEVI:v10p296/r7.anchor: حسن بصري قدس سره : كفت كساني را يافتم كه ايشان بدنيا جوانمرد وسخى بودند

BURSEVI:v10p296/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p296/r8.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p296/r8.claim: Al-Qashani reads the reward as enduring traces and attributes in the garden of soul and heart, free from corruption and materiality.
BURSEVI:v10p296/r8.anchor: لهم أجر من ثواب الآثار والصفات فيج نة النفس والقلب غير مقطوع

BURSEVI:v10p296/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p296/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p296/r9.claim: Inwardly, those believing from spirit, secret, heart, and spiritual powers, and doing good by turning from the world toward God, receive reward through God’s grace and mercy rather than self-effort or self-congratulation.
BURSEVI:v10p296/r9.anchor: إلا الذين آمنوا من الروح والسر والقلب وقواهم الروحانية وعملوا الصالحات من الأعراض عن الدنيا

QASHANI:84:23-25/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:84:23-25/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:84:23-25/r2.claim: Believers purify their hearts from psychic traits and acquire virtues through righteous deeds; their reward in the gardens of self and heart is unending and immaterial.
QASHANI:84:23-25/r2.anchor: الإيمان العلمي بتصفية قلوبهم عن كدر صفات النفس وتزكيتها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#11/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#11/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#11/r1.claim: غير ممنون means not cut off.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r1.claim: One analysis makes the exception disconnected from the pronoun in “give them glad tidings”: the glad tidings to the damned are sarcastic, while “except” introduces a contrasting group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r1.anchor: وقيل : هو استثناء منقطع من ضمير { فبشرهم } فهو داخل في التبشير المستعمل في التهكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r2.claim: The disconnected exception's illa functions like “but”; defining istidrāk as removing an assumed implication is only an approximate definition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r2.anchor: فحرف { إلا } بمنزلة ( لكن ) والاستدراك فيه لمجرد المضادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r3.claim: The promise of an unblemished reward answers how the believers fare; a generous reward carries honor and no reproach, since reminding recipients of a favor spoils it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r3.anchor: والأجر غير الممنون هو الذي يعطاه صاحبه مع كرامة بحيث لا يعرض له بمنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r4.claim: Al-Nābigha's verse describes one blessing after another as free of the sting of reproach; al-Zamakhsharī says blessings taste sweeter than reminders of favors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r4.anchor: علي لعمرو نعمة بعد نعمة لوالده ليست بذات عقارب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r5.claim: Alternatively, ghayr mamnūn means uninterrupted, from the verb for cutting a rope, as in the description of fruit in 56:32–33.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās tells Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq that ghayr mamnūn means uncut; he cites al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza's use of manīn for dust left behind after a fast-moving rider.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p235/r6.anchor: سأل نافع بن الأزرق الخارجي عبد الله بن عباس

NAHHAS:v5p188/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p188/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p188/r8.claim: الذين is accusative as an exception from the pronoun suffix, but may instead be a detached exception.
NAHHAS:v5p188/r8.anchor: الذين في موضع نصب استثناء من الهاء والميم ويجوز أن يكون استثناء ليس من الأول

NAHHAS:v5p188/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p188/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p188/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says an elderly person who became weak after doing good deeds in strength is credited with the same reward for what he used to do.
NAHHAS:v5p188/r9.anchor: كما روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس إلا الذين آمنوا قال الشيخ الكبير إذا كبر وضعف وقد كان يعمل شيئا من الخير

NAHHAS:v5p188/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p188/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p188/r10.claim: غير ممنون means that God does not remind them of his favor as a reproach.
NAHHAS:v5p188/r10.anchor: قال ( لهم أجر غير ممنون ) أي لا يمن به عليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r5.claim: The exception is disconnected: rather, believers inwardly and doers of good outwardly receive afterlife reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r5.anchor: هذا استثناء منقطع، يعني لكن الذين آمنوا-أي: بقلوبهم-وعملوا الصالحات بجوارحهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says their reward is not diminished; Mujahid and al-Dahhak say uncounted, together meaning uninterrupted, as in another verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r6.anchor:
غير منقوص. وقال مجاهد، والضحاك: غير محسوب.
وحاصل قولهما أنه غير مقطوع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddi reports views that their reward is not diminished or is not a favor owed to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم: {غير ممنون} غير منقوص. وقال بعضهم: {غير ممنون} عليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects denying God’s favor to Paradise’s people: they enter by grace and mercy rather than deeds, and remain recipients of His favor eternally, praising Him as naturally as breathing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p361#2/r8.anchor: وإنما دخلوها بفضله ورحمته لا بأعمالهم، فله عليهم المنة دائما سرمدا

QURTUBI-FULL:84:22-25/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:22-25/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:22-25/r7.claim: The exception is disconnected: those affirming both testimonies and fulfilling obligations receive undiminished, uninterrupted reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:22-25/r7.anchor: { إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات } استثناء منقطع، كأنه قال: لكن الذين صدقوا

QURTUBI-FULL:84:22-25/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:22-25/r8.speaker: نافع بن الأزرق وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:84:22-25/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains ghayr mamnūn as uncut or uninterrupted, citing Arabic usage; another view says the reward is not held over them as a favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:22-25/r8.anchor: وسأل نافع بن الأزرق ابن عباس عن قوله «لهم أجر غير ممنون» فقال: غير مقطوع.

STUDYQURAN:84:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r1.claim: The verse may be read with “but” to distinguish believers' fate from that of disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r1.anchor: Some say this verse should read, “but those who believe . . .” to distinguish the fate of believers from that of disbelievers

STUDYQURAN:84:25/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r2.claim: Alternatively, “save those who” distinguishes disbelievers who repent from those who do not.
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r2.anchor: Others say that it should be “save those who . . .” to distinguish the disbelievers who repent from those who do not

STUDYQURAN:84:25/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r3.claim: For “reward unceasing,” the commentary refers readers to 41:8 and 95:6.
STUDYQURAN:84:25/r3.anchor: For the meaning of reward unceasing, see 41:8c; 95:6c.

SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r1.claim: If لهم أجر is a new or circumstantial clause, the exception of those who believe may be either connected or disconnected.
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r1.anchor: هذا إذا كانت الجملة من قوله: " لهم أجر " مستأنفة أو حالية. أما إذا كان الموصول مبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r2.claim: If the relative clause is the subject and لهم أجر its predicate, the exception is disconnected rather than an exception of individuals: the believers instead have such-and-such reward.
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r2.anchor: فالاستثناء وليس من قبيل استثناء المفردات، ويكون من قسم المنقطع، أي: لكن الذين آمنوا لهم كيت وكيت

SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r3.claim: The meaning of ممنون was explained earlier under Sūrat Fuṣṣilat, at 41:8.
SAMIN-DURR:84:25/r3.anchor: وتقدم معنى " الممنون " في حم السجدة

TAB-FULL:v24p259/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r1.claim: The believers who do good works receive a reward that is neither counted nor diminished.
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {لهم أجر غير ممنون}

TAB-FULL:v24p259/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses their reward as undiminished.
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r2.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {لهم أجر غير ممنون} [الانشقاق: 25] يقول: غير منقوص "

TAB-FULL:v24p259/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses their reward as uncounted.
TAB-FULL:v24p259/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {أجر غير ممنون} [الانشقاق: 25] يعني: غير محسوب "

TABATABAI:84:24-25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:24-25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:24-25/r2.claim: The exception for believers who do good is disconnected from the pronoun in the command to announce punishment; their reward comes without a burdensome reproach.
TABATABAI:84:24-25/r2.anchor: والمراد بكون أجرهم غير ممنون خلوه من قول يثقل على المأجور.

TABRISI:84:24-25/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:24-25/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:84:24-25/r2.claim: The believers' reward is neither diminished nor cut off because the bliss of the Hereafter does not end.
TABRISI:84:24-25/r2.anchor: أي غير منقوص ولا مقطوع لأن نعيم الآخرة غير منقطع عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:84:24-25/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:24-25/r3.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:84:24-25/r3.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the reward is neither diminished nor clouded by reproach; the same is related from al-Hasan.
TABRISI:84:24-25/r3.anchor: غير منقص ولا مكدر بالمن عن الجبائي وروي ذلك عن الحسن

TABRISI:84:24-25/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:24-25/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:24-25/r4.claim: The phrase may also mean there is no favor or claim over them for what they earn; the root of “favor” means cutting, as when a rope is severed, illustrated by Labīd's poem.
TABRISI:84:24-25/r4.anchor: وأصل المن القطع يقال: مننت الحبل إذا قطعته قال لبيد

TABRISI:84:24-25/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:24-25/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:24-25/r7.claim: The statement that God sees him follows the denier's assumption he will not return: rather, he will return and God will requite his deeds.
TABRISI:84:24-25/r7.anchor: لما أخبر عن ظن الكافر أن لن يحور عقبه بالإخبار بأنه يحور

TABRISI:84:24-25/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:24-25/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:24-25/r8.claim: Alternatively, it means he will return to the Hereafter, where his Lord sees his state and will recompense him.
TABRISI:84:24-25/r8.anchor: بلى سيرجع إلى الآخرة وربه بصير بأحواله فسيجازيه بأعماله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p375/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p375/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p375/r1.claim: Muqātil says the exception is for believers drawn from the unbelievers mentioned earlier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p375/r1.anchor: مقاتل: استثنى من آمن من الكفار بقوله: {إلا الذين آمنوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p375/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p375/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p375/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās says the unending reward is neither diminished nor cut off, since the bliss of the afterlife grows and continues.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p375/r2.anchor: غير منقوص ولا مقطوع؛ لأن نعيم الآخرة يزيد وينمو (¬4)، ولا ينقطع

ASAD-NOTES:84:24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:84:24/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:84:24/r1.claim: A warning of grievous future suffering is excepted for those who repent, believe, and do good works, whose reward will be unending.
ASAD-NOTES:84:24/r1.anchor: unless it be such [of them] as [repent, and] attain to faith, and do good works: for theirs shall be a reward unending!

ELMALILI:84:22-25/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:22-25/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:22-25/r5.claim: The exception is generally disconnected when believers are excepted from disbelievers, but connected with respect to believers who had been among the disbelievers.
ELMALILI:84:22-25/r5.anchor: istisnâ-yı munkatı‘olursa da kâfirler içinden iman edenlere nazaran muttasıldır

ELMALILI:84:22-25/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:22-25/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:22-25/r6.claim: For those who believe and do good, an ungrudged reward means either a reward without indebtedness because earned, or an eternal reward that never ceases.
ELMALILI:84:22-25/r6.anchor: mennolunmaz, yani kendi kesbleri olmak itibariyle minnetsiz, yahut kesilmez ebedî

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p248/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p248/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p248/r3.claim: If people enslaved to worldly love refuse the Qur'anic path, the Prophet should warn them of deserved torment; only faith and righteous deeds bring salvation and eternal reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p248/r3.anchor: Only those people will be saved from this torment

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p377/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p377/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p377/r4.claim: The believers who do good receive a reward that is neither cut off nor diminished.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p377/r4.anchor: لهم أجر غير ممنون} غير مقطوع ولا منقوص.

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r7.claim: The exception can be connected or disconnected and means those who repent and believe; their reward is uninterrupted or not held over them as a favor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r7.anchor: استثناء منقطع أو متصل، والمراد من تاب وآمن منهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r8.claim: A Prophetic report promises that readers of al-Inshiqāq will be spared receiving their book from behind their backs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r8.anchor: من قرأ سورة الانشقاق أعاذه الله أن يعطيه كتابه وراء ظهره

JISHUMI:v10p7346/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the believers’ reward as not diminished.
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r11.anchor: قيل: غير منقوص، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v10p7346/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r12.claim: Another interpretation is that the reward is not cut off.

JISHUMI:v10p7346/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r13.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r13.claim: Abu ʿAli says the reward is not marred by reproach or reminders of generosity.
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r13.anchor: وقيل: غير منغص بالمن، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7346/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r14.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r14.claim: Abu Muslim identifies the reward as Paradise.
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو الجنة، عن أبي مسلم.
